sections.h2: Is it better to list or sell as-is in Irondequoit?
sections.html:
It comes down to the house's condition and your calendar. Irondequoit is a Rochester suburb that grew fast after World War II, so the roof, the furnace and the basement often decide which route pays more.

Homes here are lived in by their owners at a rate of 78.8%, and the midpoint value is $182,500, so one large repair can take a real bite out of a sale. Get a contractor quote or two before listing. Modest work favors a regular listing. Heavy work, a vacant or inherited house, or back taxes can favor an as-is sale that stops the carrying costs.

  • Agent listing: the widest audience, with commission, showings and lender approval attached.
  • Owner sale: you keep the commission and run the marketing, haggling and paperwork.
  • As-is cash sale: fewer contingencies and a date you can often pick, usually at a lower price.

Put every bid in writing with the price, closing date, proof of funds and closing costs, then compare what each would leave you.

sections.h2: Where is Irondequoit and how did it grow?
sections.html:
Irondequoit sits in north-central Monroe County between the Genesee River on the west and Irondequoit Bay on the east, with the Lake Ontario shoreline on the north. Water borders it on three sides, which makes it a headland. The City of Rochester lies south and west, and Penfield, Webster and Brighton touch it on the east and southeast.

The boundary with Rochester is odd. A thin strip of city land runs north along the east bank of the Genesee, and the northern half of Durand Eastman Park, along with Seneca Park, belongs to the city, not the town. If your address says Irondequoit but you are close to those parks, check the tax bill to see which municipality actually taxes the house.

The town was set off from Brighton in 1839. In the late 1800s its lakefront was a tourist area for Rochester residents, once called the Coney Island of Western New York. After World War II the population climbed from 23,376 in 1940 to 55,337 in 1960 as returning veterans looked for homes. The West Irondequoit and East Irondequoit central school districts serve the town, and its colonial-style Town Hall dates to 1951.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show for Irondequoit homeowners?
sections.html:
About 50,200 people live in the town, 1.7% fewer than at the 2020 base. About 22.6% of residents are 65 or older, so some sales follow a downsizing move or an estate.

sections.h2: When are Irondequoit property taxes due?
sections.html:
The Receiver of Taxes collects Town, County and School taxes through the Tax Office. Town and County bills are mailed on the last business day of December and are due February 10. School bills are mailed on the last business day of August and are due October 1.

When a due date lands on a day the town offices or post office are closed, the town accepts payment on the next business day without penalty. State law says that missing a bill does not excuse the tax, and the office says it cannot forgive penalties. If a non-escrow owner has not received a bill within a week of mailing, the Tax Office at 585-336-6050 will send a copy, and the Monroe County website shows bills too.

To look up a parcel, use Monroe County's Real Property Portal: agree to the disclaimer, enter the house number and street, then open the Pay Property Taxes icon to view school and combined town and county statements and the payment history. Print the current statements for your closing attorney.

sections.h2: What are the key assessment dates for Irondequoit owners?
sections.html:
The town lists eight dates that shape every owner's tax bill, and a sale does not stop any of them. Knowing them helps you time a listing.

  • March 1: taxable status date and last day for new and renewal exemption applications.
  • May 1: tentative roll becomes public, with a paper copy at Town Hall.
  • Third Tuesday in May: school budget vote.
  • Fourth Tuesday in May: Grievance Day.
  • July 1: final roll and valuation date. A judicial review (SCAR hearing) can be requested within 30 days after the final roll date.
  • Early September and early January: school and Town and County bills are mailed.

Because the final roll sets the next September school bill and January Town and County bill, a buyer who closes in summer inherits the assessment you see on that roll. Look at it before you set a price.

sections.h2: How does a grievance work in Irondequoit?
sections.html:
You file an application with the Assessor's Office between May 1 and Grievance Day, the fourth Tuesday in May. The 2026 hearing was held on May 26, 2026, so the next one is the fourth Tuesday in May 2027, which is May 25, 2027. Filing a grievance is a first step, and you must complete it before you can ask for a small claims review.

The town asks for one original of Form RP-524 plus four copies, with supporting documents for each board member. Hearings need an appointment, and in 2026 the paperwork for a hearing was due a week before Grievance Day. The assessor's tentative figure is presumed correct, so you carry the burden of proof. Credible evidence includes a recent appraisal, a purchase contract, a list of recent sales of similar homes or a broker's written opinion of value. Tax information is not accepted as evidence of value.

The assessor may offer a stipulation before the hearing. You can accept or reject it, and accepting locks in the agreed assessed value. If you are unhappy with the board's decision, a Small Claims Assessment Review through Monroe County Supreme Court costs $30 under Section 730 of the Real Property Tax Law. The town also ran informal review appointments in March and April of 2026 and publishes a comparable sales book built from sales dated 7/1/2024 to 7/1/2025.

sections.h2: What does the transfer tax cost, and where is the deed recorded?
sections.html:
The state's transfer tax runs $2 for each $500 of price, owed by the seller unless the contract moves it. At the town's midpoint home value of $182,500, that comes to $730, from 365 units of $500.

It is reported on Form TP-584, and residential sales of $1 million or more also owe a 1% tax that the buyer pays. Deeds for Irondequoit are filed with the Monroe County Clerk at 39 W. Main Street, Room 101, Rochester, NY 14614, which is the registrar of deeds, mortgages, satisfactions of mortgages, judgments and liens. Your closing attorney or title company usually handles the filing.

sections.h2: What should I check before accepting a cash offer in Irondequoit?
sections.html:
Add up what you keep after every cost, then think about the calendar. A listing with a higher price can lose that edge to commission, repairs and months of mortgage, tax and utility bills.

  • Confirm in writing who pays the transfer tax and closing costs.
  • Ask for proof of funds and a firm closing date.
  • Print current statements from the Monroe County portal so unpaid tax is settled at the table.
  • Compare against a listing price opinion from a local agent.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day in Irondequoit?
faqs.a: It is the fourth Tuesday in May, which falls on May 25, 2027 for the next one. Applications are accepted from May 1 through Grievance Day, and hearings need an appointment.

faqs.q: When are Irondequoit property taxes due?
faqs.a: Town and County taxes are due February 10, and School taxes are due October 1. If a due date falls on a closed day, payment is accepted the next business day without penalty.

faqs.q: How much does a small claims assessment review cost in Irondequoit?
faqs.a: The filing fee is $30 under Section 730 of the Real Property Tax Law, and the review is handled through Monroe County Supreme Court. You must go through the town grievance first.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax when an Irondequoit house sells?
faqs.a: The seller pays New York's $2 per $500 tax unless the contract says the buyer will. A separate 1% tax applies to residential sales of $1 million or more, and the buyer pays it.

faqs.q: Is Seneca Park part of Irondequoit?
faqs.a: No. Seneca Park and the northern half of Durand Eastman Park belong to the City of Rochester, even though they sit along the town's western and northern edges. Check your tax bill if your house is close to them.
